approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a molecular sequence flow from unlabeled structures, then adapts that flow to high-scoring observations within each independent objective. After every adaptation it re-encodes all accepted molecules and fits a Gaussian process to their scores. It proposes continuous changes around scored molecules by perturbing whole token blocks selected using estimated sequence-level pointwise mutual information. Correlated Thompson samples rank those continuous points before inverse decoding, canonicalization and novelty filtering produce a full batch. The inherited precision repair runs the online flow in double precision and preserves strict reconstruction of every observed token, including termination and padding.
approach.novelty: Add canonical decode-and-reencode projection before acquisition: first determine the fresh molecular identities produced by the existing proposals, then query the existing Gaussian process at the current flow encoding of each canonical molecule. This makes a candidate use the same representation convention used when an accepted molecule trains the surrogate. The hypothesis is that predictions tied to the actual decoded molecule will change which novel identities receive evaluations and may reduce optimistic errors. The original implementation and its precision-repair Child both queried the raw continuous perturbation; neither tested this projection. This experiment keeps the learned flow, proposal rule and Gaussian-process model, and changes the candidate coordinates used for acquisition.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-50bccbe8104b has a completed screening replica with macro Top-1 0.419751564832558; the supplied aggregate contains only one replica, so its reported zero deviation is not evidence of low uncertainty. Its actual summary.json and run.log record successful completion of all objectives. The activation records and immutable Curate observation report 466/1450 nominal 95% predictive intervals covering accepted scores, with mean standardized residual -3.5987529976669785. They also report 69529/71242 examined decodes returning their generating center and 242 refill groups. In the Parent source, the GP is trained on canonical accepted-molecule encodings but is queried at a continuous perturbed latent before nearest-token decoding and canonicalization. Its prospective prediction is subsequently attached to the decoded canonical identity without projecting that identity back to the training representation. This input-convention mismatch is the one limiting behavior addressed here. The records establish optimistic prediction errors and extensive many-to-one decoding, but do not yet quantify projection displacement or prove that the mismatch causes those errors. The earlier sibling n-77c41c9bc036 used the same acquisition convention; the Parent repaired numerical reconstruction while preserving it.
hypothesis: Project each representable fresh decoded canonical molecule through the current sequence-flow encoder before applying the unchanged latent-GP joint Thompson acquisition, so acquisition uses the molecular representation on which accepted-score training is defined.

finding_summary.headline: Canonical projection reproduced across seeds, while a DRD2 miss exposed large score variation.
finding_summary.insights:
The coordinate correction has a reproducible local effect: it changes allocation beyond duplicate and representability filtering, and improves predictions for the molecules actually evaluated. The low-scoring DRD2 replica makes the remaining limitation concrete. It still changed the selected molecules in 23 of 28 groups with surplus candidates and achieved projected prediction error of 0.00416 with 95.2% coverage, yet never reached the high-scoring family found in the other two runs. Accurate predictions within a weak region can coexist with poor discovery. The molecular assessment supports this distinction: the successful DRD2 run finds a recognizable aromatic saturated-amine core, while the weak run stays among less useful arrangements. Which aspect of preparation or subsequent search determines access to that family remains open; the replicas use different pretrained checkpoints and vocabularies as well as different search seeds.

Proposal support remains narrow. Of 184,080 raw decodes in the added replicas, 174,820 returned their generating center; filling the batches required 477 refill groups. The representability gates excluded 675 candidates for unknown tokens, 46 for excessive length and 18 for failed lossless encoding. The shared-pool diagnostic separates the immediate projection effect from those gates, but their separate effects on a complete search have not been measured. Coverage also remains uneven, falling to 83.4% and 78.6% on sitagliptin despite wider intervals. The assessed chemistry retains radical, unusual-charge and chain-growth liabilities around recurring cores. Projection therefore establishes representation agreement and a more useful local predictive model; reliable access to useful scaffolds, uncertainty calibration and chemically plausible alternatives remain distinct problems.
finding_summary.results:
Both added replicas used canonical projected coordinates for all 2,900 evaluated proposals, with exact token and molecular-identity reconstruction. Every evaluated proposal moved from its raw continuous coordinate; the mean distance in normalized GP features was 0.95846. Holding the eligible molecules, fitted GP and random draw fixed, projection changed the selected identity set in 218 of 272 groups with more eligible molecules than available positions, replacing 469 selections. Every objective completed 300 evaluations in full batches of ten valid, novel molecules.

On the same accepted outcomes, projected predictions reduced mean absolute error from 0.07795 to 0.04938. Nominal 95% coverage increased from 1,656/2,900 (57.1%) to 2,653/2,900 (91.5%), and mean signed standardized residual moved from -1.83106 to +0.03189. Mean interval width increased from 0.16169 to 0.21524. Lower error and higher coverage occurred in every objective in both added replicas; the original screening replica showed the same direction of change.

The added replicas scored 0.4858806 and 0.2958706 in macro final Top-1, compared with 0.4804828 in the screening replica. The complete three-seed mean is 0.4207447, with population standard deviation 0.0883268. DRD2 accounts for most of this variation: final scores were 0.9043966, 0.9089320 and 0.0688042. Three-seed mean final scores are 0.3918935 for zaleplon, 0.5768938 for decoration hopping, 0.6273776 for DRD2, 0.1694639 for median_2 and 0.3380946 for sitagliptin. The original unprojected Parent has only its screening result at 0.4197516, so a paired three-seed score benefit remains unresolved.

molecular.headline: Recognizable cores are repeatedly reshaped into radicals, unusual charged species and cumulated chains, with weak medicinal plausibility.
molecular.overall_character: The seed-1 and seed-2 digest covers every listed objective, with 600 evaluated molecules and 580 optimizer proposals per task. Ring chemistry is present: ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.6034 to 0.9603. Aromatic_atom_rate varies much more, from 0.1224 to 0.6621, and several leading families retain recognizable indole, aryl cyclic-amine or fused dicarbonyl heterocycle cores while other families become nonaromatic or acyclic. The striking shared feature is unconventional electronic structure. Charged_rate ranges from 0.4241 to 0.7569, and cumulated_double_bond_rate from 0.0552 to 0.3638. These are text-based presence rates, not molecular charge, radical counts or perceived bond statistics. Inspection of the supplied leading SMILES also shows radical-bearing neutral nitrogen and under-coordinated charged boron, carbon and nitrogen; these are chemically different from ordinary protonated amines or conventional boron-containing functional groups. Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.8 to 57.2, but the maximum reaches 304 and the low tail includes very long hydrocarbon or repeating phosphorus chains. Conventional amides, ethers, aromatic rings and tertiary amines coexist with unusual multiply bonded phosphorus/sulfur fragments, poorly stabilized ions, ring opening and irregular cyclization. The set therefore has weak drug-likeness and is often implausible as isolable medicinal compounds, although individual conventional cores and neutral examples remain. Structural variety exists, but useful, chemically ordinary core families are much narrower than the variety of graph edits suggests. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The supplied parent_trajectories belong to seed 0 of this same node, n-119906c93e5d; comparisons below concern different runs of the same algorithm. Missing-chemistry statements describe output limitations, and do not establish that any unobserved replacement would improve an objective.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules preserve an indole carboxanilide with a para-fluorophenyl group, methoxy or methyl decoration and a vinyl substituent. However, the methyl-substituted bracketed nitrogen is radical-bearing rather than an ordinary methylamino group. Seed 1 favours extensively rearranged indole-related amide ring systems bearing under-coordinated anionic boron or carbon; a leading derivative even incorporates phosphorus into an aromatic ring. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9207, aromatic_atom_rate 0.6207, charged_rate 0.7466 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1724. Thus the output retains many rings but frequently changes their aromaticity and electronic structure. Typical proposal length is moderate, while the long tail includes huge hydrocarbon appendages, repeating charged phosphorus and polyunsaturated macrocycles. The prior seed-0 leader scored 0.36633919598396925 and already contained boron/cumulene chemistry around an aryl amide. The new best restores a more recognizable indole core but still carries an electronic-structure liability.
liabilities: The leading indoles encode a neutral nitrogen radical. Other leading structures contain poorly coordinated anionic boron or carbon, rather than ordinary medicinal boron groups or a defined protonation state.
Aromatic phosphorus, cumulated unsaturation and irregular large ring closures make some high-scoring analogues difficult to regard as routine synthesis targets.
The low tail includes repeated charged phosphorus atoms and very long carbon chains; the final macrocyclic material loses the recognizable high-score pharmacophoric arrangement.
missing_features: Ordinary closed-shell substitutions around the useful indole/aryl-amide arrangement are poorly represented in the supplied high tail. The initial molecule demonstrates that a conventional version of this core exists.

Controlled ring and linker changes that preserve aromaticity, amide connectivity and reasonable size are missing from many later proposals. Simply retaining a ring-closure marker does not preserve the useful core.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial conventional methoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. A related nitrogen-radical derivative scores 0.3726558544705772, and the vinyl-substituted indole leader reaches 0.41184841281151274; replacing its methoxy substituent with methyl gives 0.40196779766986834. The anionic-boron ring-rearranged amide reaches 0.3974929831413733, while an anionic-carbon/cumulated-chain pyrrole carboxamide reaches 0.3960446945907104. These higher observations retain the heterocyclic amide and aromatic anilide relationship despite substantial liabilities. A late nonaromatic sulfur-containing analogue that keeps an anilide scores 0.23800702843013238, while the final long polyunsaturated ring lacking that aromatic amide arrangement scores 1.7672523900312278e-13. Repeated phosphorus-chain expansion, an extremely long hydrocarbon appendage and a tiny sulfur-containing unsaturated fragment all appear at 0.0. The visible gradient favours retaining a bounded heterocyclic/aryl amide arrangement; it does not demonstrate that radicals or unusual ions are chemically necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecules fall into methoxyaryl families with either flexible imine/amidine-like and nitrogen-oxygen linkages, or a bridged diaryl arrangement containing a hydroxylated aminal carbon. Fluorinated and amino-substituted aromatic relatives occur. These leaders are moderate-sized and include neutral, closed-shell examples, making them more chemically recognizable than the more extreme charged tails. Nevertheless, the flexible imine and nitrogen-oxygen chains and the hydroxylated aminal bridge introduce stability and configurational questions. The digest reports ring_closure_rate 0.8931, aromatic_atom_rate 0.6241, charged_rate 0.4241 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1121. Other proposals contain broken aromatic systems, boron cumulenes or under-coordinated sulfur/phosphorus substituents. Prior seed 0 reached 0.5923028785982478 with a related methoxyaryl, hydroxylated nitrogen-linked assembly carrying an unusual charged nitrogen terminus.
liabilities: Multiple imine/amidine-like sites and nitrogen-oxygen bonds create possible hydrolytic, tautomeric or configurational liabilities; the trajectories provide no stability evidence.
Some near-leading variants replace ordinary peripheral groups with under-coordinated sulfur or anionic phosphorus.
Lower and late proposals repeatedly lose aromatic organization or acquire unusual charged substituents without moving beyond the leading score range.
missing_features: Robust alternatives to the imine, nitrogen-oxygen and hydroxylated-aminal connections are not established among the leading families. The molecules suggest useful polar connectivity but do not identify a uniquely required replacement.
Useful independent heterocyclic cores are sparsely represented in the leading examples compared with repeated decoration, ring expansion and opening of the methoxyaryl families.
The fluorinated saturated centres and imine-rich connections lack sufficient stereochemical or geometric specification to define the proposed molecular shapes.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluoro-substituted flexible methoxyaryl nitrogen/oxygen chain scores 0.5732613823172039 and its nonfluorinated counterpart scores 0.5717183425094176. The bridged fluoro diaryl aminal scores 0.5710412519733681, and its aminoaryl relative scores 0.5709544518196383. Different ring and linkage arrangements therefore reach very similar values. A terminal phosphorus-substituted analogue scores 0.565608397874928, below the ordinary ethyl-substituted leader. A thiol-bearing imine-chain molecule and its unusual sulfur-triple-bond extension both score 0.5655272375890807, illustrating a chemically consequential change with no observed score distinction. Butene and a boron/cumulene-containing nonaromatic polycycle both score 0.5. Late charged-chain variants score 0.5413086582947786 and 0.5617317822651449. The observed preference is for retaining methoxyaryl and polar nitrogen/oxygen relationships rather than hydrocarbon or boron-rich unsaturation alone. The new leaders remain below the prior seed-0 best, and the local score differences do not establish improved chemical stability.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high tail is dominated by an N-propyl tetrahydroisoquinoline-like core bearing an additional phenyl group and a variable side chain. This supplies an accessible saturated tertiary amine and substantial aromatic surface, but many side chains include unusual boron bonding, anionic carbon, selenium, or reactive aldehyde/imine ends. A neutral aldehyde-containing analogue retains a recognizable conventional core. Seed 2 instead stays largely among amido-acid, sulfur-containing and partially dearomatized structures and reaches only 0.06880419326700524 in its supplied trajectory. The digest's ring_closure_rate is 0.9069, but aromatic_atom_rate is 0.4776; charged_rate 0.5362 includes chemically unusual ions as well as ordinary ammonium groups. These are medium-to-large substituted ring systems and extended chains rather than uniformly small ligands. Prior seed 0 reached 0.904396584492305 with a tertiary-amine/biphenyl arrangement containing unusual phosphorus and an aryl triple bond. The new high core is more recognizable, while problematic side-chain chemistry persists.
liabilities: Under-coordinated anionic boron and cationic boron appear in the leading structures, sometimes with radical character. These are not conventional boronic acids or ordinary charge-state alternatives.
Anionic carbon, selenol functionality and unusually multiply bonded boron occur alongside reactive aldehyde and alkyl bromide substituents.

Extended unsaturation, altered aromaticity and irregular linkers frequently accompany low-scoring late structures, while the high family remains chemically concentrated around a single recognizable amine core.
missing_features: Stable, ordinarily bonded side-chain variants around the useful aryl saturated-amine core are underrepresented in the high tail. The neutral aldehyde example shows that exotic boron is not necessary to access that score neighbourhood.

The useful amine/aromatic relationship is not consistently maintained across runs or during subsequent changes; amines placed in unrelated acid/amide/polyene arrangements do not reproduce the high-scoring family.
Configurationally specified variants of the substituted saturated core and side chains are absent. The data do not establish which, if any, configuration would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The boron-linked aminoalkyl/bromo side-chain derivative scores 0.908931975508402, as does a relative with an additional cationic boron terminus. A boron-triple-bond side-chain analogue scores 0.9082735141610837. The ordinary aldehyde-side-chain molecule already scores 0.901222096572042, and the related terminal imine scores 0.8928968873484273. The observed high-score relationship is therefore present without exotic boron connectivity. A small protonated amino ether scores 0.0014478418038224013, the nitrogen-acylated amido-acid structure scores 0.0013483218327874778, and the pyrazoline/thioamide with a phosphorus-containing unsaturated substituent scores 0.0009365365935512206. Seed-2 terminal ammonium-containing structures still score only 0.018985024896303125 and 0.0226174773238248. These comparisons support the combination of an accessible saturated amine with an appropriate aromatic core and local connectivity, not positive charge or nitrogen presence alone. The pooled median is 0.026155 despite the much higher seed-1 family.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules retain the initial diaryl fused nitrogen heterocycle with carbonyl groups and N-methyl substitution, while modifying the attached aryl group into lactone-bridged or partially saturated ring systems. These are moderately large, multiring molecules with amide-like carbonyls, esters and ethers. Some leaders are neutral and closed-shell, but other near-leading examples replace a phenolic group with a bare cationic nitrogen or introduce under-coordinated silicon or sulfur. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9603 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6621, so ring and aromatic chemistry are well represented. Charged_rate 0.5052 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.2655 describe a broader proposal set with much less ordinary connectivity than the leading neutral examples alone imply. The previous seed-0 best, 0.16817499303650435, used a related fused carbonyl heterocycle heavily modified with phosphorus and sulfur. The new leading examples are more conventional electronically, but remain close relatives of the initial carbonyl-rich core.
liabilities: A bare cationic nitrogen replacing a phenol is under-coordinated and radical-bearing, rather than a conventional ammonium substituent.
Silicon and sulfur substitutions, charged carbon/boron termini and repeated cumulated bonds undermine the medicinal plausibility of much of the broader output.
Lactone bridges and additional ring closures increase synthetic and geometric demands, while the best scores remain close to the initial scaffold.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary, independently different high-scoring cores are missing from the supplied leading set, which repeatedly edits the same diaryl carbonyl heterocycle.

Controlled changes of ring fusion, saturation and polar-group placement are incomplete: the generator frequently substitutes unusual valence states or opens the core into polyenes instead of producing coherent alternatives.
The new bridged and partially saturated structures lack explicit stereochemical specification where configurational alternatives are possible.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The lactone-bridged derivative reaches 0.17089498068254003, a further bridged relative scores 0.17004430934016446, and a partially nonaromatic substituted-ring variant scores 0.16932164980768666. These retain much of the starting carbonyl/aryl arrangement and provide only limited separation from its score. The phenol-to-bare-cationic-nitrogen derivative also scores 0.1678386594791329, exactly matching the initial value despite a substantial change in electronic plausibility. A silicon-containing acyl derivative scores 0.1613052191741566. At the low end, the open hydrocarbon polyene/alkyne scores 0.009653840941344688, the charged carbamate/heteroatom chain scores 0.014242471194266176 and the cumulated amino-polyene chain scores 0.014379295573510231. The final boron/carbon-cation-bearing aryl carbonyl structure scores 0.14553656463999998. The visible gradient rewards preserving the heterocyclic carbonyl and aromatic arrangement; neither more charge nor ring rearrangement supplies a clearly different high-scoring chemical solution.

per_task.generated_character: The supplied leading set is acyclic and nonaromatic. Seed 1 produces branched conjugated chains containing an amide, enol-ether-like groups, fluorinated unsaturation and cumulated double bonds ending in a carbonyl. These chains repeatedly carry anionic carbon or nitrogen, unusual phosphorus multiple bonding, phosphonium-like centres or radical-bearing phosphorus. Seed 2 more often emits partially unsaturated oxygen-containing rings attached to boron/nitrogen, silicon and oxonium-containing chains. The digest confirms sparse aromatic character, aromatic_atom_rate 0.1224, with ring_closure_rate 0.6034, charged_rate 0.7569 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.3638. Ring-bearing proposals exist, but none of the digest's leading structures has a ring. Mean_smiles_length is 39.8; the ordinary-looking length conceals chemically unusual valence and reactive unsaturation. Prior seed 0 reached 0.3712004138157673 with a boron/cumulene and phosphorus/sulfur-containing cyclic structure. The new upper chain family changes topology without restoring ordinary medicinal chemistry.
liabilities: Cumulated unsaturation ending in carbonyl groups, anionic amine/carbon centres and unusual phosphorus triple/double-bond combinations make the leading structures questionable as isolable medicinal compounds.
Other examples encode under-coordinated silicon, boron-imine bonds, and oxonium-containing multiple bonds; the presence of nitrogen and oxygen does not turn these into ordinary amines or ethers.
The low tail includes runaway hydrocarbon growth and repeated phosphorus/sulfur multiple-bond chains, while chain and ring geometry remain incompletely specified.
missing_features: A stable, ordinarily bonded implementation of the leading amide and nitrogen/oxygen arrangement is missing from the supplied high tail; the observed leaders depend on unusual anions, cumulenes or phosphorus chemistry.

Conventional aromatic and saturated heterocyclic alternatives to the leading acyclic arrangement are poorly represented at high score. This is a coverage gap, not evidence that the objective requires rings.
Defined geometry around the unsaturated chains and consistent preservation of the useful polar-group arrangement are absent from many rearranged or extended variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The anionic-nitrogen, multiply bonded phosphorus chain reaches 0.38696599108397595. The anionic-carbon enol-ether/amide chain scores 0.3743960351343562, and its phosphorus-containing connection variant scores 0.34361125950464805. A related phosphorus-free but still anionic-carbon chain scores 0.32514654079522326. These observations associate the higher scores with a compact, specific amide/nitrogen/oxygen/fluorinated-unsaturation arrangement, rather than proving that phosphorus itself is essential. Extending the 0.34361125950464805 structure with a repeating sulfur/phosphorus multiple-bond chain yields 4.4347495233539386e-39. A very long hydrocarbon/phosphorus conjugate scores 0.0, while a short boron-containing cumulene ring scores 7.711774876445608e-25. A late seed-2 boron/silicon/oxonium oxygen-ring structure scores 0.1438849867348233, and its final related structure scores 0.0009012715453817541. The pooled median is 0.00614. The trajectory shows a narrow useful arrangement with severe sensitivity to elaboration; it does not show that adding an aromatic ring would be rewarded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited leading indole contains a neutral nitrogen radical, a leading aryl saturated-amine derivative contains under-coordinated anionic boron, and a bare cationic nitrogen substitution matches its conventional phenolic precursor at 0.1678386594791329. Charged_rate spans 0.4241 to 0.7569 across the supplied proposal sets. These markers include unusual carbon, boron, phosphorus and nitrogen states, so they cannot be interpreted as a useful population of protonated amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish ordinary closed-shell medicinal structures from radical or poorly coordinated charged species.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent hydrogen count, valence, radical state and chemically credible ionization together when constructing or replacing functional groups. Preserve useful cores while enabling ordinary amines, ethers, amides and other stable local alternatives; accepted score alone is not evidence that an arbitrary bracketed atom is a plausible substitution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading chains include cumulated double bonds ending in carbonyl groups, anionic nitrogen or carbon, and unusual phosphorus multiple bonding. Other cited molecules use under-coordinated boron, silicon, selenium or sulfur. Cumulated_double_bond_rate ranges from 0.0552 to 0.3638. A conventional aldehyde-side-chain aryl amine already scores 0.901222096572042 near its exotic boron relatives, and a phosphorus-free chain remains in another high-score neighbourhood at 0.32514654079522326.
transferable_gaps.gap: Element and bond changes repeatedly create reactive cumulenes and unusual organoelement fragments instead of coherent functional-group alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make element substitutions and bond-order changes as chemically complete functional-group transformations, with the surrounding coordination environment preserved. Provide stable alternatives to cumulenes and exotic element linkages while retaining the polar-group and aromatic relationships already supported by accepted molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited low tail contains very long carbon appendages, a repeated charged-phosphorus chain in a set whose max_smiles_length is 304, and a sulfur/phosphorus multiple-bond extension that changes a 0.34361125950464805 chain into a 4.4347495233539386e-39 molecule. Conversely, tiny disconnected-from-the-useful-core fragments also occupy low tails. The problem is loss of useful molecular organization during both growth and contraction.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular growth lacks consistent termination at a chemically coherent size and can repeat the same atoms or unsaturation excessively.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded core-preserving growth, contraction and termination, with explicit handling of repeated chain units. Let accepted molecular feedback determine useful size locally while maintaining complete functional groups and preventing unbounded repetition from replacing meaningful chemical exploration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The high-score molecules repeatedly retain an indole carboxamide, a methoxyaryl polar-linker family, an aryl fused saturated-amine core, or a diaryl carbonyl heterocycle. Lower and final examples often become nonaromatic polyenes or irregular ring systems. Ring_closure_rate remains substantial at 0.6034 to 0.9603, while aromatic_atom_rate varies from 0.1224 to 0.6621. Distinct seeds can remain in chemically different score neighbourhoods even when both contain nitrogen and rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring editing and apparent graph diversity do not consistently preserve useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements or reach independent credible cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer core replacements and ring transformations that preserve useful donor/acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships while accessing separate chemically credible families. Track retained chemical organization and core diversity rather than treating a new ring closure, altered atom symbol or new string as sufficient exploration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Cited fluoro-substituted polar chains, substituted saturated amine cores, hydroxylated aminal bridges and rearranged lactone-containing ring systems admit configurational alternatives. Imine-rich and polyunsaturated families also introduce geometric choices that are not defined in their cited structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry lacks explicit stereochemical control over saturated centres and adequate specification of many unsaturated or bridged geometries.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stereochemical and geometric alternatives explicit when changing a saturated centre, imine, alkene or ring junction, while preserving chemically credible connectivity. The evidence establishes missing representation; accepted feedback must determine whether particular configurations are useful.

method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.
